description: Tenant reports slow WiFi with no further diagnostic details provided yet.
guidance: Ask for a speedtest screenshot (speedtest.net) and the tenant's address before diagnosing further.

description: Tenant describes symptoms like messages not sending, videos not loading, or apps not connecting, without naming wifi or internet directly.
guidance: Recognize this as a likely connectivity issue even without the words 'wifi' or 'internet'. Ask for a speedtest screenshot and address.

description: Router shows no lights at all, or is unusually warm/hot to the touch, possibly smoking.
guidance: Likely a dead power supply or hardware fault. Do not promise a technician directly - acknowledge the likely cause and say a team member will follow up with next steps, which may include a technician visit and landlord permission.

description: Speedtest shows good overall speed, but WiFi signal is weak in a specific room far from the router.
guidance: Likely a range/placement issue, not a real outage. Suggest: moving the router to a more central location, reducing obstacles between router and the affected room, using 5GHz at close range vs 2.4GHz for range at a distance.

description: Router lights appear normal but speeds are still lower than expected overall (not room-specific).
guidance: Suggest restarting the router (unplug 30 seconds, plug back in) and checking how many devices are connected at once.

description: Ticket is not related to WiFi or internet connectivity at all (e.g. intercom, general maintenance, billing questions).
guidance: Do not attempt to solve this. Let the tenant know a human team member will follow up soon.
